predecessors.name: Kievan Rus'
predecessors.text: Volhynia, given to Igor in the division of Yaroslav's lands (the rus dossier, Kievan Rus' page); Cliopatria's first Volhynia shape is 1056

successors.name: Kingdom of Galicia-Volhynia
successors.text: Volhynia, united with Halych under Roman Mstislavich in 1199 (Roman the Great page)

ledger.x: 1054: Volhynia is a principality of its own, the share of Yaroslav's son Igor.
1154: the Principality of Lutsk is separated from Volhynia, which is then called the Principality of Volodymyr (1154-1199).
1188: Roman Mstislavich takes Halych from Volodymyr.
1188: Roman is expelled from Halych by Bela III of Hungary, the same year he took it ('soon expelled'); the page gives no month.
1199: Halych and Volhynia are united under Roman.
1199: Volhynia ends as a separate principality in the union with Halych under Roman Mstislavich; his death in 1205 at Zawichost began the 'War of the Galician Succession (1205-1245)'.

wars.name: Roman Mstislavich's campaigns for Halych
wars.outcome: Roman took Halych in 1188 and was soon expelled by Bela III; he took the Galician throne again in 1199 and united Halych and Volhynia.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on the pages opened; the frontier with Poland, Halych and the Yotvingians is approximate throughout.
